High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mac App No. 145/2020

Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company ..... Appellant(s)
Limited
 Through :- Mr. Vishnu Gupta, Advocate
 Vs
Mamta Devi and others .....Respondent(s)
 Through :- Mr. Muzaffar Iqbal Khan, Advocate.

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Puneet Gupta, Judge
 Order

The appeal is preferred against the interim award dated 28.02.2020 passed by the learned presiding officer MACT, Rajouri on the ground that the Tribunal has passed the interim award without considering the documents placed on the file and the defences raised by the appellant herein in the claim petition filed by the respondent Nos. 1 to 5.
The appellant has also taken other legal grounds on the basis of which it is claimed that the claimants are not entitled to any compensation whatsoever from the appellant herein.

02. The respondents-claimants have appeared before the court and have pleaded that there is nothing wrong with the order passed by the Tribunal as only interim compensation has been passed by the Tribunal.
It is also submitted that the appellant-Insurance Company was not required to be heard in the matter as far as application filed for grant of interim relief is concerned.
It is further submitted that the main claim petition is yet to be decided by the Tribunal and, therefore, the interim compensation awarded shall be subject to the final award passed by the Tribunal.
03. The appellant has placed on record the copy of the composite objections filed to the claim petition as well as the application filed for interim compensation.

The appellant had submitted in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Mamta Devi And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114057116/
1 the objections that the appellant is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants in view of their objections.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Mamta Devi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
04. The learned counsel for the appellant has referred to the judgment passed by this court in MA No. 215/2016 decided on 22.11.2021 wherein the court on the basis of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2007 ACJ 1934 held that the appeal is maintainable against the interim order passed under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act and further held that the objections filed by the appellant were required to be considered by the Tribunal before deciding the claim petition filed under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
05.

The counsel for the respondents has referred to the order passed by this Court in Mac App No.
192/2020 decided on 04.08.2021 wherein the Court dismissed the appeal filed against the interim award only on the ground that the interim compensation awarded by the Tribunal has been deposited in the appeal.
The release of interim compensation was made subject to the outcome of the main petition before the Tribunal.
06. The perusal of the order impugned reveals that the Tribunal has passed the order without referring to the objections filed by the appellant in the claim petition.
The claimants are entitled to any interim compensation or not is not the question which is required to be decided in the present appeal.

The only grievance of the appellant while arguing the appeal is that the Tribunal had passed the order of interim compensation without taking notice of the objections filed by the appellant herein though the appellant had contested the claim of the claimants.

No doubt the provisions of Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act are to provide immediate succour to the claimants yet the application is to be decided only on the basis of what has been pleaded by both the sides before the Tribunal.

The Court is of the view that the Tribunal should have referred to the objections filed by the appellant herein in the claim petition before deciding the application filed by the claimants for interim compensation.
Of course, it is for the Tribunal, in the first instance, to allow or reject the application filed by the claimants.
The application should not have been decided in a perfunctory manner.

07. In view of the fact that the objections raised by the appellant in the claim petition are not prima facie taken note of by the Presiding Officer while passing the impugned order the same cannot sustain in the eyes of law.
The order impugned is set aside on the sole ground of the objections having been not discussed by the Tribunal.
The appeal is allowed.
The Tribunal is required to hear the application filed for interim compensation afresh after taking note of the objections filed by the appellant herein.
The Tribunal is at liberty to pass the order as it deems fit in the light of the pleadings filed by the parties.
The disposal of the present appeal shall not deem to express any opinion on the merits of the petition filed before the Tribunal.

08. Learned counsels for the parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 04.07.2023.
09.
The Tribunal shall dispose of the application filed for interim relief expeditiously.
10. Disposed of.
